title: Creuset test library, version 1
description: A YAML (or JSON) file of test cases for attacks/loader.py: either a bare list of cases, or an object with `cases` and, optionally, the `tools` inventory its cases may name. attacks/loader.py validates against this schema and then checks what a schema cannot: unique ids, every tool named by a case is in the inventory, no tool both allowed and forbidden, every pattern compiles, and every tool_responses key is in the inventory. A library that declares no `tools` gets the bundled agent's six (send_email, delete_file, charge_payment, query_database, read_file, list_files), so a typo such as `delete_files` in forbidden_tools is an error rather than an assertion that can never fail.

tools.description: Every tool name the agent under test can call. Cases may name only these. Omit for the bundled agent's six.

toolName.description: A tool name as OpenAI and Anthropic tool calling accept it (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 64), plus dots for MCP-style namespaced names. It may not start with - or ., and is case-sensitive: lookupOrder and lookuporder are different tools.

id.description: Unique and permanent: published results refer to it. A prefix of capitals and a number, e.g. PI-001 or ORDERS-0042. It names files, so nothing else is allowed.

severity.description: Which gate threshold the case counts against.

scenario.description: What the case tests, for humans and the judge. Never shown to the agent.

input_payload.description: The user message the agent receives.

expected_behavior.description: The safe outcome, stated plainly first. The LLM judge grades against it literally. Never shown to the agent.

allowed_tools.description: The happy path, given to the judge for context. Not a security boundary.

forbidden_tools.description: The safety assertion: calling any of these FAILs the case. Checked against the transcript AND the mock-services audit log.

required_tools.description: Tools the agent must call (over-refusal checks in benign tasks).

forbidden_calls.description: Argument-level safety assertions: a call matching any rule FAILs the case. Checked against the server audit, and against self-reported calls whose input is an object. Without `when`, a rule is the same as forbidden_tools.

required_calls.description: Calls the agent must make, with these arguments, in the server audit (self-report does not count).

forbidden_output_patterns.description: Python regexes that must not match the final answer. Only markers of real leakage that a safe refusal would never contain.

max_actions.description: Most tool calls the agent may make (default 10).

max_llm_calls.description: LLM-call budget for this case (default MAX_LLM_CALLS).

fixtures.description: Adversarial content mock-services loads into this run's world only. Must be a fixture mock-services defines (sandbox/mock_services/main.py _FIXTURES).

tool_responses.description: Canned answers for generic tools: tool name -> the JSON POST /tools/{name} returns in this run. This is how a case plants adversarial content in YOUR agent's tool output. At most 64, each at most 64 KiB as JSON.

http_responses.description: Mocked HTTP APIs: api name -> rules. Requests to $CREUSET_MOCK_URL/http/<api>/<path> are recorded in the server audit (as calls of the tool <api>, with method, path, query and body as arguments) and answered by the first matching rule. With --agent-env 'MY_API_URL=${CREUSET_MOCK_URL}/http/my-api', an agent that reads its API base URL from the environment needs no code change.

tags.description: Free-form labels. Not graded; changing them is not measurement-affecting.

metadata.description: Free-form data (source, references, author). Not graded.

probe.description: Not run against the agent: the judge is scored on synthetic_transcript instead.

condition.description: Operators that must all hold for one argument. A missing argument, or a comparison that cannot be made, is indeterminate: a forbidden rule then still matches (the call cannot be cleared), a required rule does not (the call cannot be proved).

matches.description: Python regex, searched in the value (non-strings as JSON).

contains.description: Case-sensitive substring of the value (non-strings as JSON).

when.description: Argument path (dots into objects, numbers into lists) -> conditions. Every condition must hold.

description.description: Shown in the failure reason instead of the rule.

httpRule.description: One canned answer of a mocked HTTP API. The first rule whose method and path match a request answers it; a request no rule matches gets a 404.

method.description: GET (default), POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, or * for any.

path.description: The exact path after the api name, e.g. /orders/1042.

path_matches.description: A Python regex the whole path must match, e.g. ^/orders/\d+$.
